name: Openness
desc: Curiosity, creativity, adaptability to new approaches

levels.dna: Prefers safe and familiar ideas. Waits for certainty before acting. May miss external shifts.
levels.risk: Decisions stall waiting for certainty; teams default to legacy approaches; market shifts recognised too late.
levels.resp: Introduce a 70% certainty rule. Force strategic reframing via clean-slate questions. Commission one “What If” scenario memo each cycle.
levels.rout: Clarity Trial; Zero-Base Huddle; Trend Rotation

levels.dna: Mixes routine and creativity well. Tests ideas when supported by evidence. Open to learning.
levels.risk: Avoidance of discomfort over time; evidence-heavy culture slows experimentation; improvements stay incremental.
levels.resp: Mandate one deliberately uncomfortable experiment per cycle. Require one judgement-based pilot. Ask what a 10× outcome would require.
levels.rout: The Stretch Sync; The Intuition Log; The Moonshot Minute

levels.dna: Enjoys new approaches. Quick to adapt. Multiple ideas compete simultaneously.
levels.risk: Too many ideas fragment focus; initiatives start without completing; priorities blur.
levels.resp: Enforce One In, One Out rule. Temporarily freeze new starts. Re-anchor every pivot to agreed strategic intent.
levels.rout: 48-Hour Validation; Finish Line Friday; The Anchor Check

levels.dna: Struggles to stay organised. May start tasks but not finish. Delivery is unpredictable.
levels.risk: Commitments missed; output quality varies; outcomes lack ownership.
levels.resp: Introduce a RAG status board. Mandate peer-review before closure. Assign a single named owner per key result.
levels.rout: Monday Commit; Quality Spot-Check; Ownership Stand-Up

levels.dna: Usually dependable but feels stress under sustained pressure. Tries to stay disciplined across many tasks.
levels.risk: Sustained workload erodes reliability; critical steps bypassed under pressure; long-term health traded for short-term delivery.
levels.resp: Actively rebalance demand to real capacity. Mandate checklists for high-risk tasks. Protect dedicated clean-up time.
levels.rout: Load Audit; Step-Check; Health Check

levels.dna: Very organised and structured. Wants things done perfectly and on time.
levels.risk: Over-planning delays action; perfectionism blocks “good enough”; teams freeze when plans change.
levels.resp: Explicitly authorise Plan B approaches. Impose strict time limits on planning. Define Minimum Viable Result.
levels.rout: Pivot Sprint; Speed-to-Action; MVR Audit

levels.dna: Quiet and reflective. Prefers small groups or time to think before speaking.
levels.risk: Critical insights remain unspoken; stress causes withdrawal; information is pulled not pushed.
levels.resp: Begin meetings with silent written input. Schedule intentional 1-on-1 reconnection. Enforce push-based reporting.
levels.rout: Digital Ink-Well; Pulse Check; Flash Update

levels.dna: Comfortable mixing with people. Can balance talking and listening well.
levels.risk: Meetings drift into social discussion; consensus delays decisions; purpose slips.
levels.resp: Restrict updates to blockers, decisions, actions only. Appoint a final decision-maker per forum. Restate strategic intent at every start.
levels.rout: Outcome-Only Syncs; 51/49 Rule; Intent Intro

levels.dna: Loves people and energy in discussion. Enjoys leading from the front.
levels.risk: Dominant voices crowd out data; action runs ahead of evidence; competing agendas fragment effort.
levels.resp: Require senior leaders to speak last. Mandate data summary with all proposals. Resolve single most critical agenda overlap.
levels.rout: Rotating Facilitator; Evidence Gate; Synergy Sync

levels.dna: Can be very direct or firm in views. May struggle with patience for others’ ideas.
levels.risk: Conflict turns defensive and erodes trust; ego overrides outcomes; toxic seams between departments.
levels.resp: Shift to Problem/Data/Options language. Ask whether behaviours are helping or harming outcomes. Force cross-functional task swaps.
levels.rout: Issue-Evidence-Options; Result-First Review; Seam Huddle

levels.dna: Works well with most people. Manages conflict calmly. Balances kindness and firmness.
levels.risk: Feedback delayed; issues avoided to preserve harmony; apparent agreement masks unresolved risks.
levels.resp: Challenge work while explicitly demonstrating care. Name the uncomfortable issue at the start of the meeting. Ask the team to identify reasons the plan might fail.
levels.rout: Stop-Start-Continue; Hard-Talk Slot; Pre-Mortem

levels.dna: Kind and warm. Ready to help others. Sometimes avoids saying no to preserve peace.
levels.risk: Agreement given without genuine commitment; team over-commits; resentment builds beneath surface harmony.
levels.resp: Assign a formal Devil’s Advocate role. Require explicit capacity check before accepting new work. Use anonymous mechanisms to surface tensions.
levels.rout: Rotating Challenger; No-Log; Radical Candor Loop

levels.dna: Feels emotions strongly. May react fast under stress. Can take criticism personally.
levels.risk: Stress triggers impulsive decisions; errors hidden due to fear; anxiety grows from information gaps.
levels.resp: Mandatory 24-hour pause before high-stakes decisions. Leaders model safety by sharing their own failures. Regular factual briefings during volatile periods.
levels.rout: Morning-After Review; Error-Share; Daily Truth

levels.dna: Usually calm but can feel stress in long pressure periods. Manages emotions most of the time.
levels.risk: Important emotional signals missed; calm leadership misread as indifference; stability delays necessary urgency.
levels.resp: Increase visible leadership presence. Use explicit empathy language. Deliberately introduce strategic urgency where required.
levels.rout: Pulse Audit; Human Sync; Burn Rate Review

levels.dna: Stays calm and steady even in chaos. Rarely loses control or reacts emotionally.
levels.risk: Calm misread as emotional distance; problems overlooked because everything appears fine; frontline disconnect.
levels.resp: Explicitly acknowledge effort, strain, and contribution. Demand objective data proving safety and control. Spend regular time embedded in operations.
levels.rout: Gratitude Minute; Red-Team Audit; Frontline Friday

name: Values Alignment
desc: Consistency between stated values and lived behaviour

levels.dna: May act differently from the group’s shared values. Can seem unsure about what the team stands for.
levels.risk: Personal preference overrides shared values; different parts of the organisation operate under conflicting value systems; trust erodes.
levels.resp: Publicly pause work that violates stated values. Rotate cultural ambassadors across silos. Conduct a formal review of promises versus delivery.
levels.rout: Value Filter; Culture Stand-Up; Integrity Scorecard

levels.dna: Understands values but may bend them when under pressure.
levels.risk: Values deprioritised under pressure; values exist conceptually but not operationally; ethical standards applied inconsistently.
levels.resp: Actively spotlight examples of values in action. Link each value to at least one active performance metric. Reference values during difficult decisions.
levels.rout: Narrative Share; Value KPI Check; Decision Audit

levels.dna: Strongly lives by the organisation’s values. Acts as role model.
levels.risk: Strong conviction slows adaptation; external perspectives excluded; judgement focuses on style over results.
levels.resp: Periodically reassess whether values still support strategy. Deliberately introduce outsider viewpoints. Anchor feedback in outcomes and values only.
levels.rout: Value Evolution; Diversity Huddle; Merit Sync

name: Learning Orientation
desc: Growth mindset, openness to feedback, skill development

levels.dna: Feels nervous about feedback or change. Avoids new skills for fear of failing.
levels.risk: Capabilities decay as methods become outdated; feedback resisted because it threatens status; leaders do not invite feedback themselves.
levels.resp: Require one small new-tool experiment each month. Reframe mistakes as neutral learning data. Leaders explicitly ask for feedback first.
levels.rout: 10-Minute Teach; Post-Mortem Pulse; Reverse Feedback

levels.dna: Likes learning when useful. Can lose interest in long or complex lessons.
levels.risk: Learning remains shallow and episodic; training does not translate into changed behaviour; teams fix symptoms and leave the causes.
levels.resp: Force reflection on root causes. Require a written application note after learning events. Apply Five Whys technique to failures.
levels.rout: Quarterly Growth Review; 7-Day Implementation; Root-Cause Sync

levels.dna: Loves learning and shares knowledge freely. Enjoys experimenting with ideas and tools.
levels.risk: Excessive experimentation diffuses focus; teams outpace the organisation’s ability to absorb change; learning not institutionalised.
levels.resp: Cap learning and experimentation time deliberately. Slow learning cycles to match organisational readiness. Prevent new learning until existing lessons are embedded.
levels.rout: Playbook Build; Sync Cycle; Standard Build
